senses.definition_en: to pay off; to be worthwhile

examples.english: I don't believe it pays off to change a huge amount of data for years of personal experience.
examples.text: No creo que salga a cuenta cambiar un montón de datos por años de experiencia personal.
examples.translation: I don't believe it pays off to change a huge amount of data for years of personal experience.

examples.english: And it worked, almost. Because that got better, but everything else got worse. So in the end it wasn't worthwhile.
examples.text: Y funcionó, casi. Porque aquello mejoró, pero todo lo demás empeoró. Así que al final no me salió a cuenta.
examples.translation: And it worked, almost. Because that got better, but everything else got worse. So in the end it wasn't worthwhile.

examples.english: Without this type of publicity, there are parts of the year where it doesn't pay off to publish a newspaper or magazine, and there are hours in which it is better not to broadcast any radio or television programme.
examples.ref: 2016, Carlos J. Campo, Periodismo de marcas:
examples.text: Sin este tipo de publicidad, hay épocas del año en las que no sale a cuenta publicar un periódico o una revista, y hay horarios en los que es mejor no emitir ningún programa de radio o televisión.
examples.translation: Without this type of publicity, there are parts of the year where it doesn't pay off to publish a newspaper or magazine, and there are hours in which it is better not to broadcast any radio or television programme.

glosses: to pay off; to be worthwhile
